name: Optical mixing
summary: Small dots or strokes of pure colour placed side by side, so that the eye mixes them at a distance.
how: Put dots of pure colour side by side; do not mix them on the palette.
Set complementary colours next to each other in the shadows.
Keep each dot under 0.5% of the picture width.

origin.note: Georges Seurat shows A Sunday on La Grande Jatte at the last Impressionist exhibition.

adoptions.via: The Autochrome plate of the Lumière brothers builds colour from dyed starch grains, and pictorialists use it for soft colour pictures.

sources.title: Michel-Eugène Chevreul, The Principles of Harmony and Contrast of Colours (1839)
